output.name: Solva

anatomy.part: torn notch at the shoulder opening
inner seam of the upper sleeve

output.myth: When Aun cut the string he was still wearing his good sleeve, the one his mother cut from her own wedding cloth. Tavo the Gale came down the cliffs that night, caught the sleeve on a gull-stake and tore it to the elbow, laughing. Aun could not climb back up the cliff with one arm of cloth hanging open to the wind, so he sat down and wept. Ennu the Kite-Wright came along with a scrap of Sil's old sail and sewed a patch over the torn place. The patch did not match. Ennu said that was the point. Hesk counted the stitches, and there were nine hundred and six, and she has never let anyone forget the number. The Torn Sleeve hangs over the Reach still, ragged at the wrist where the Gale got his fingers in. If you are mending something and it will not match, do not unpick it. A mended thing can still hold wind.
